$comment: PURPOSE AND SHAPE: This recipe projects stable identity and short queryable facets into properties while keeping ATT&CK's long-form prose in the Markdown body. PROPERTIES: title + technique_id + stix_id + url are identity (curie is emitted automatically from source.ontology plus the leaf filename stem). domain, tactics, platforms, data_sources, is_subtechnique, technique_version, defenses_bypassed, permissions_required, effective_permissions, impact_type and supports_remote are the short, clean, enumerable facets the techniques sheet supplies; these are what Bases tabulates and what the Tier 2 projection indexes. parent is the single clean sub-technique-of link; render() already omits a managed value that renders as "[[]]" (src/render/index.ts), so the 203 top-level techniques get no broken parent. BODY: description (656/656 rows, median ~1,250 chars), detection (582/656) and system requirements (36/656, real sentences) are prose and belong in the body, one section each at heading_depth 2. Empty cells are dropped by the body_entry omit_if_empty default, so a technique without a detection paragraph gets no empty Detection heading. PROPERTIES-VS-BODY RATIONALE: a 1,000-word ATT&CK description in YAML is unreadable in Obsidian's property panel, awkward to escape, and invisible to body search; a 14-value tactic facet is useless in the body and essential in properties. No body projection repeats the note's own filename or identifier: the engine already writes an H1 ahead of every recipe body region (buildDefaultBody on the recipe path, composeDocumentBody on the wizard path), so a recipe-side title heading would be a duplicate. SOURCE BINDING: retargeted from a STIX bundle shape ({external_references.0.external_id}, {id}) to the tracked Frameworks/enterprise-attack-v16.1.xlsx `techniques` sheet, which is the corpus this project actually ships and fingerprints against. The layout mechanism and destination structure are unchanged: one flat file per technique named by its technique id, so T1548.md is still T1548.md. The column set is byte-identical between enterprise-attack-v15.1.xlsx and v16.1.xlsx, so source.version is deliberately not declared. The xlsx parser reads with raw:false, so Excel booleans arrive as the formatted text "TRUE"/"FALSE"; is_subtechnique and supports_remote therefore carry a `lower` filter so the emitted values are the lowercase "true"/"false" a Bases filter would be written against (the closed filter set has no boolean cast, so these stay YAML strings). Every non-required column carries the leading `optional` filter so a future release that drops a column degrades to an omitted key instead of failing the row. RIGHTS: MITRE grants a non-exclusive, royalty-free license to use ATT&CK for research, development and commercial purposes, conditioned on carrying MITRE's copyright designation and the license text into each copy. The required notice, verified against https://attack.mitre.org/resources/legal-and-branding/terms-of-use/ on 2026-08-26, is: "(c) 2026 The MITRE Corporation. This work is reproduced and distributed with the permission of The MITRE Corporation." MITRE ATT&CK and ATT&CK are registered trademarks of The MITRE Corporation. Because the generated notes reproduce ATT&CK descriptions verbatim they ARE copies under that license, so the final body projection appends the notice to every note. Corpus provenance and rights posture: https://cybersader.github.io/crosswalker/reference/framework-corpus/. FACET LISTS: tactics, platforms and data_sources are emitted as real YAML arrays through {<column>|optional|split(,)}, so Bases facets them instead of matching substrings inside a comma-joined string. Measured on enterprise-attack-v16.1: 14 distinct tactics across 852 assignments (up to 4 per technique), 10 platforms across 1,629 (up to 9), and 106 data sources across 2,049 (up to 18); no item on any of the three contains a comma, so one delimiter splits all of them cleanly. This was recorded here as a blocking gap until 2026-08-26: the only splitter in the grammar was managed_links, which force-wrapped every piece in [[...]] and would have minted roughly 800 links to 14 tactic notes this recipe does not create. The per-item transformation capability removed that coupling — split produces a list, the sink decides whether the items become links — so the facet is emitted as plain values and the tactic hub notes stay the job of the registry's recommendedEnrichment facetNotes hint, which is where they belong. STILL SCALARS, DELIBERATELY: defenses_bypassed, permissions_required, effective_permissions and impact_type are also comma-delimited, and the same one-token change would list them, but they are sparse (104, 122, 19 and 32 of 656 rows) and defenses_bypassed is unnormalized — it carries 'Anti Virus' alongside 'Anti-virus' and 'Application Control' alongside 'Application control', so faceting it would present near-duplicate values as distinct facets. Converting a facet is cheap; presenting a dirty facet as a clean one is not, so these wait on a normalization step rather than riding along. KNOWN GAP 1 (mitigation prose needs a two-hop join, which is producer work by design) - MITRE keeps mitigations in a separate `mitigations` sheet (44 rows) joined to techniques through the `relationships` sheet (18,570 rows, mapping type `mitigates`). That is technique -> relationships -> mitigations: TWO hops. source.joins (SchemaVer 1.9.0) is keyed lookup enrichment, not relational algebra, and is fixed at depth 1 on purpose - in a second hop the key depends on the first hop's result set rather than on the primary row, which is a join operator composing with another join operator and brings back join ordering, intermediate cardinality explosion, and an unbounded memory story. Two-hop is therefore ruled OUT of scope for source.joins, in v1 and permanently under this design; the stated fallback is that a producer denormalizes the two sheets into one, or emits valid Tier 1 directly. What IS expressible today is hop 1 alone - joining `relationships` on ID = `source ID` filtered to `mapping type` = 'mitigates' and selecting `target ID` - which would give a technique note the IDENTIFIERS of its mitigations (M1047 and so on) as a list, ready for managed_links. Identifiers yes, prose no. That half-close is not adopted here either, because it changes what a note CONTAINS rather than which rows become notes, and it is a separate decision. graph_edges remains schema-reserved and ignored until v0.2. No mitigation prose is emitted. KNOWN GAP 2 (no CURIE for the parent) - parent_curie is deliberately NOT emitted alongside parent. The engine mints each note's curie itself, and neither minting path yields mitre-attack:T1548 for this source: defaultCurieLocalPart (src/generation/generation-engine.ts:2372) matches only lowercase row.curie/id/subject_id/control_id/code and so falls back to row-N for a sheet whose id column is `ID`, and the wizard path derives the prefix from the resolved ontology id rather than from the recipe. A hardcoded {sub-technique of|curie-prefix(mitre-attack)} would therefore dangle. The wikilink resolves unconditionally because the flat layout names every file by its technique id, so the clickable half is emitted and the queryable half waits on recipe-declarable identity. DELIBERATELY DROPPED: `relationship citations` (up to 22,250 chars of "(Citation: X),(Citation: Y)" with empty leading pieces, meaningless without joining the 3,885-row `citations` sheet - see gap 1); `contributors` (semicolon-delimited credits with commas inside individual items, so neither delimiter splits cleanly, and it is neither a queryable facet nor reader-facing prose); `created` and `last modified` (non-ISO date text such as "15 October 2024" that the closed filter set cannot normalize, so it would sort lexically and mislead anyone treating it as a date - source drift is already tracked by _crosswalker.concept_cid).
